brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Four full hex bases at (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (-1,0) level 0, closed with caps on open faces and joints bolted; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.
Notch drawer frame (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) at (-1,1), filling the empty position between bases (-1,0), (0,0) and (0,1).

requirements.requirement: A spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: Mount spike spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 at the junction of bases (0,0), (0,1), (1,0).

setSpikeAccessory platform-sm on the mount spike (a solid spike refused platforms, so it was swapped for a mount spike). Platform was accepted with no warnings; I did not visually confirm it in a render because the look call framed nothing.

finish.summary: Built a small level-0 desk unit: four hex bases, a male-female notch drawer frame in the pocket between three of them, and a mount spike at the corner where bases (0,0), (0,1) and (1,0) meet, carrying a small platform. Open faces are capped and joints bolted; check_build is clean with meshClash clear. No drawer contents or desk props were added since the brief asked only for the structure.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
